Who We Are

About SWANA

The South-West Asia and North Africa (SWANA) Palliative Care Association is a professional and advocacy body dedicated to advancing palliative and end-of-life care across one of the world's most diverse and underserved regions.

The SWANA region is home to more than 600 million people spanning more than 20 countries, each with distinct languages, cultures, healthcare systems, and challenges. Despite this diversity, our communities share a common need: compassionate, dignified care for people facing serious illness and their families.

SWANA was founded by a community of dedicated practitioners and advocates who recognised that regional collaboration, shared knowledge, and collective advocacy are essential to building sustainable palliative care systems across the region.

The SWANA Region

Our association represents and serves practitioners, institutions, and patients across Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Syria, Tunisia, Turkey, the UAE, Yemen, and neighbouring countries.

This is a region of extraordinary richness — in culture, language, history, and human resilience. It is also a region where palliative care services remain underdeveloped, where suffering from serious illness is often inadequately addressed, and where much work remains to be done.

Our Purpose

Mission, Vision & Values

Mission

To convene and connect palliative care stakeholders across the SWANA region, build regional capacity, advance evidence-based practice, and advocate for the integration of palliative care into health systems — ensuring compassionate, culturally sensitive care for all who need it.

Vision

A region where every person facing serious illness and every family has access to high-quality, culturally grounded, compassionate palliative care — as a recognised and protected right.

Values

Compassion, dignity, cultural humility, equity, collaboration, evidence-based practice, and a commitment to the voices of patients and families.

Strategic Priorities

Regional Networking

Building a connected community of palliative care professionals, educators, and advocates across the region.

Education & Training

Developing and delivering culturally adapted educational programmes, webinars, and professional development resources.

Research & Evidence

Promoting regional research, sharing evidence-based practices, and building a knowledge base tailored to SWANA contexts.

Policy & Advocacy

Advocating for palliative care integration in national health policies, essential medicines access, and recognition at regional and international levels.

Capacity Building

Supporting institutions and healthcare systems to develop sustainable palliative care services across the region.

Public Awareness

Raising awareness among the public, policymakers, and health systems about the importance of palliative care.
